What is the Arazzo Specification? Frank Kilcommins: Module 4: Modeling API Workflows with Arazzo

(3) What is the Arazzo Specification?

  • The Arazzo Specification is a community-driven open specification within the OpenAPI Initiative, a Linux Foundation Project
  • Arazzo describes an approach to document use-case oriented workflows in a programmatically readable format
  • A workflow is a series of API calls which when woven together accomplish a specific task or goal or business objective
  • The human-readable nature improves the ability of API specifications to tell the story of the API(s) in a manner that can improve the consuming developer experience.
  • The machine-readable nature allows for intent orientated workflows to be discoverable and executable by AI agents, testing tools, documentation tools, and so on!


What is the Arazzo Specification? Frank Kilcommins: Module 4: Modeling API Workflows with Arazzo

(4) Dominant Use Cases

  • Deterministic recipes for the use of APIs
    • Make sense of large unwieldy API description
    • Bridge the gap where business flows span more than one API description
  • Living API documentation and improved consumer developer experience (DX)
  • Assertable business value (machine readable end-to-end test semantics)
  • Targeted code generation tooling (think SDKs, MCP Servers) for APIs driven by use cases
  • Improved regulatory checks via assertable workflows
  • The AI potential for value orientated repeatable interaction with APIs

Arazzo Specification 1.1 Updates Frank Kilcommins: Module 4: Modeling API Workflows with Arazzo

(29) Arazzo Specification 1.1 - Just Released!

What's new:

  • AsyncAPI support
  • Chained workflow execution
  • Advanced JSONPath / XPath selector support
  • OpenAPI 3.2 alignment
  • Precision improvements:
    • Full ABNF grammar
    • Truthy/Falsy condition semantics
    • And more!


Arazzo Specification 1.1 Updates Frank Kilcommins: Module 4: Modeling API Workflows with Arazzo

(30) Arazzo 1.1 - AsyncAPI Support

  • Source Description Object [https://spec.openapis.org/arazzo/v1.1.0.html#source-description-object] now supports the following document types:
    • openapi
    • arazzo
    • asyncapi


Arazzo Specification 1.1 Updates Frank Kilcommins: Module 4: Modeling API Workflows with Arazzo

(31) Arazzo 1.1 - AsyncAPI Support

  • Step Object references operations (or channels) described in AsyncAPI Document using operationId or channelPath.
  • Async steps define an action (“send” or “receive”) indicating message flow intent.
  • A correlationId in AsyncAPI links a request with its response, and must be in-sync with the AsyncAPI Document.
  • A timeout sets the maximum number of milliseconds to wait for the step to complete before aborting and failing the step.


Arazzo Specification 1.1 Updates Frank Kilcommins: Module 4: Modeling API Workflows with Arazzo

(32) Arazzo 1.1 - AsyncAPI Support

  • Step Object now has the ability to specify explicit dependencies.
  • These are a list of steps that MUST be completed before the current step can be executed.
  • dependsOn only establishes a prerequisite relationship for the current step and does not trigger execution of the referenced steps.


Arazzo Specification 1.1 Updates Frank Kilcommins: Module 4: Modeling API Workflows with Arazzo

(33) Arazzo 1.1 - Chaining Workflows

  • Action Objects now fully support chaining workflows, and mapping workflow inputs using the parameters fixed field.


Arazzo Specification 1.1 Updates Frank Kilcommins: Module 4: Modeling API Workflows with Arazzo

(34) Arazzo 1.1 - Advanced Selector Support

  • A new Selector Object [https://spec.openapis.org/arazzo/v1.1.0.html#selector-object] which is usable across workflow outputs, step outputs, requestbody payloads, parameter values, payload replacement values.
  • Enables fine-grained traversal and precise data selection from structured data such as JSON or XML, using a defined selector syntax such as jsonpath, xpath, or jsonpointer.
    • The context sets the root node for the selector.
    • The selector specifies the expression.
    • The type specifies the selector syntax.


Arazzo Specification 1.1 Updates Frank Kilcommins: Module 4: Modeling API Workflows with Arazzo

(35) Arazzo 1.1 - Selector Expression Types

  • Overriding the default Selector Expression versions via the Expression Type Object [https://spec.openapis.org/arazzo/v1.1.0.html#expression-type-object] (renamed from Criterion Expression Type Object)
    • Specify the type and version for the selector expression to override default


Arazzo Specification 1.1 Updates Frank Kilcommins: Module 4: Modeling API Workflows with Arazzo

(36) Arazzo 1.1 - Selector Expression Type Defaults



Arazzo Specification 1.1 Updates Frank Kilcommins: Module 4: Modeling API Workflows with Arazzo

(37) Arazzo 1.1 - OpenAPI 3.2 Alignment

  • The Parameter Object [https://spec.openapis.org/arazzo/v1.1.0.html#parameter-object] has a new querystring option for the in fixed field, which treats the entire URL query string as a single value.


Arazzo Specification 1.1 Updates Frank Kilcommins: Module 4: Modeling API Workflows with Arazzo

(38) Arazzo 1.1 - Identity-Based Referencing

  • To ensure interoperability, when referencing an Arazzo Description by URI, references MUST use the target document’s $self if present.
  • $self is a URI-reference for the Arazzo Description ensuring portable and unambiguous reference resolution.


Arazzo Specification 1.1 Updates Frank Kilcommins: Module 4: Modeling API Workflows with Arazzo

(39) Arazzo 1.1 - Housekeeping

  • ABNF Expressions
    • Complete grammar
    • Clarity on string embedding
    • Source Description resolution ordering
  • Truthy/Falsy evaluation semantics for conditions
  • Tool listing added to ReadMe (also see openapi.tools [https://openapi.tools/collections/arazzo])


Arazzo Specification 1.1 Updates Frank Kilcommins: Module 4: Modeling API Workflows with Arazzo

(40) Arazzo: Looking Ahead to 1.2, 1.3, ... , 2.0

  • SOAP support (already merged into 1.2 branch)
  • gRPC, GraphQL, MCP, A2A step support
  • Actor-in-the-loop support (human or agent)
  • Function / transformation support
  • Loop support

Example Travel Workflow Use Case Frank Kilcommins: Module 4: Modeling API Workflows with Arazzo

(43) Example Travel Workflow Use Case

A concierge-grade workflow for rebooking disrupted flights for Platinum and Ultimate passengers, rebooking hotels, and arranging transportation

Steps:

  • Retrieve rebooking options based on loyalty profile
  • Confirm selected offer and create shopping cart entry
  • Fetch full confirmed offer details
  • Modify hotel reservation (if arrival date not honoured)
  • Resolve hotel location - Overture Maps via PlaceId
  • Request luxury ride pickup for 30 mins after arrival
  • Confirm ride details and pickup ETA for customer support
  • Return consolidated itinerary


Example Travel Workflow Use Case Frank Kilcommins: Module 4: Modeling API Workflows with Arazzo
